subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: One essay on a poetry or prose text
Analysis of language, form and structure
Use of textual references and quotations

questions.q: Within the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Literature (4ET1) specification, what is the assessment type of Component 3?
options: An externally examined written paper
Coursework
A speaking and listening endorsement
A multiple-choice reading test
questions.explain: Component 3 of the 4ET1 specification is the internally assessed coursework option.

questions.q: How many essays does a student produce for the English Literature coursework component?
options: Two contrasting essays
One essay
Three short responses
Four themed assignments
questions.explain: The coursework requires a single essay responding to one text.

questions.q: The coursework essay must be written in response to which type of text?
options: A drama text only
A poetry or prose text
A non-fiction media text
A film adaptation
questions.explain: The specification requires one essay on a poetry or a prose text.

questions.q: What proportion of the overall International GCSE English Literature qualification does the coursework component contribute?
questions.explain: The coursework component is weighted at 40% of the total qualification.

questions.q: How is the English Literature coursework assessed?
options: Marked by an external examiner in an exam hall
Internally marked by the centre and externally moderated by Pearson
Peer-marked by other students only
Not marked, only submitted for records
questions.explain: Coursework is assessed internally by the teacher and then externally moderated by Pearson.

questions.q: Assessment Objective 1 (AO1), central to the coursework, requires students to develop what?
options: A comparison between two contrasting texts
An informed personal response, using textual references including quotations
An understanding of historical context above all else
A creative rewriting of the text's ending
questions.explain: AO1 asks for a critical style and an informed personal response supported by textual references and quotations.

questions.q: Assessment Objective 2 (AO2) requires students to analyse which features used by a writer?
options: Language, form and structure
Grammar, punctuation and spelling
Setting, weather and food
Title, cover and blurb
questions.explain: AO2 focuses on how language, form and structure create meanings and effects.

questions.q: According to the assessment objectives, how should students support their interpretations in the coursework essay?
options: With personal anecdotes from their own lives
With textual references, including quotations
With diagrams and illustrations
With references to other students' essays
questions.explain: AO1 requires interpretations to be supported and illustrated with textual references, including quotations.

questions.q: What does producing a 'personal and critical response' primarily involve?
options: Retelling the plot of the text in your own words
Developing your own informed interpretation supported by evidence
Describing how the text made you feel emotionally, without evidence
Summarising what critics have said, without your own view
questions.explain: A personal and critical response means offering your own evidenced interpretation rather than mere summary or unsupported opinion.

questions.q: Which of these best characterises a 'critical style' as expected in the coursework?
options: Analytical and evaluative writing about the text
A descriptive retelling of events in order
A negative attack criticising the author personally
A list of the characters and settings
questions.explain: A critical style means analysing and evaluating the text, not simply describing or narrating it.

questions.q: Why are quotations important in the coursework essay?
options: They increase the word count quickly
They provide textual evidence that supports and illustrates the student's points
They show the student has memorised the whole text
They replace the need for the student's own analysis
questions.explain: Quotations serve as evidence that supports interpretations, a key AO1 requirement.

questions.q: AO2 asks students to use 'relevant subject terminology'. Which of the following is an example of such terminology?
options: Metaphor
Paragraph
Sentence
Chapter
questions.explain: Literary terms such as metaphor allow precise analysis of a writer's craft, as required by AO2.

questions.q: What distinguishes analysis from summary in a coursework essay?
options: Analysis explains how and why techniques create effects, whereas summary just states what happens
Analysis is longer than summary
Analysis avoids using any quotations
Analysis lists events in chronological order
questions.explain: Analysis examines the effects of a writer's choices, while summary merely restates content.

questions.q: What does it mean for a personal response to be 'informed'?
options: It is based on close reading and understanding of the text
It is written quickly without planning
It is based only on feelings, with no reference to the text
It copies the views of a published critic
questions.explain: An informed response is grounded in close reading and genuine understanding of the text, not unsupported opinion.

questions.q: Which approach to using quotations is most effective in an analytical essay?
options: Embedding short, well-chosen quotations smoothly into sentences
Copying long paragraphs of the text without comment
Using a quotation only in the introduction
Paraphrasing rather than quoting so no quotation marks are needed
questions.explain: Concise, embedded quotations integrated into analysis show precise engagement with the text.

questions.q: Why does focusing the coursework on a single poetry or prose text benefit the student?
options: It allows a detailed, developed and sustained analysis of one text
It means less reading is required overall
It removes the need to use quotations
It guarantees a comparison mark
questions.explain: A single-text essay enables the depth of sustained personal and critical analysis the coursework rewards.

questions.q: Which sentence best demonstrates AO2 analysis of language?
options: The poet describes a storm at the start of the poem.
The violent verb 'crashed' conveys the storm's destructive power, mirroring the speaker's inner turmoil.
There is a storm in the poem which is quite dramatic.
The poem is about a storm and the sea.
questions.explain: This response names a technique, uses terminology and analyses its effect, meeting AO2.

questions.q: A student writes about a novel's protagonist. Which sentence shows the strongest personal and critical response?
options: I think the character is nice and I liked reading about him.
The character does lots of things in the story.
Arguably, the writer presents the protagonist's silence as quiet resistance, inviting the reader to question who truly holds power.
The protagonist is the main character of the book.
questions.explain: It offers an evidenced, interpretive personal judgement about the writer's presentation, the hallmark of a critical response.

questions.q: Which of these is the best example of an embedded quotation supporting a point?
options: The writer creates a sense of confinement, describing the room as a 'cage' that traps the heroine.
Here is a quotation: 'cage'. This is important.
The room is a cage. That is what the book says on page forty.
The heroine feels trapped. Quote to follow later in the essay.
questions.explain: The quotation is smoothly embedded within a point about the writer's effect, integrating evidence and analysis.

questions.q: Given a coursework task asking how a poet presents loss, which essay plan best meets the assessment objectives?
options: Retell the events of the poem verse by verse from start to finish.
Structure analytical paragraphs around methods, each analysing language, form or structure with embedded quotations and a personal interpretation.
Write only about the poet's biography and the year the poem was published.
List every literary term you know and define each one in turn.
questions.explain: Organising around the writer's methods with evidence and interpretation directly addresses AO1 and AO2.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Literature (4ET1) specification; Coursework
